title: Starting on the Ellington charter tour at the William Penn Theater
summary: Asked for one big-band experience, Green picks the Duke Ellington charter beginning in Pittsburgh, with the Berry Brothers on the bill.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Okay, let's move on -- let's move on to the big band era and those different places that you used to perform. Just give me one of the places and tell me about that experience -- the band that you were with, arriving there, what it was like, who was there, what kind of show it was, what was the format of the show, and would you travel by bus to get to a place generally, and when you arrived there where would you stay, was there any discrimination between blacks and whites --
Well, tell me about one of those whole experiences -- one in particular.
Well, the most important was the Duke Ellington one, yousee, because that was a charter. We had to go up into -- outside of this town, I think it's called -- oh,
yeah, at the William Penn -- William Penn Theater -- That's in Pittsburgh. Well, they (unintelligible)
Well, I say in the days of 'The March of Times.'
Yeah, it was a famous year in the early '40's, right -- the late '30's, that's where we're at.
So, you were with the Duke Ellington Band with Chuckles.
Well, there was the Berry Brothers.
